 Parma vs AS Roma: Donyell Malen Goal Gives Giallorossi 1-0 Lead, Dybala in Spotlight
 AS Roma leads 1-0 against Parma thanks to a Donyell Malen goal in the first half of their Serie A match at Ennio Tardini Stadium, with Paulo Dybala returning to the starting lineup.
 By: Damar Prasetya 
 | 
 Editor: Nayla Savitri 
 November 22, 2026 at 1:56 AM WITA ·
 5 min read
 AS Roma striker, Donyell Malen, celebrates a victory over Parma at Ennio Tardini Stadium on May 10, 2026. Archive photo from a previous match. Photo credit: AS Roma 
 PARMA, Aktualita.co -  AS Roma gained an important advantage in their match against Parma during the 12th week of the 2026/2027 Italian Serie A season. Playing at Ennio Tardini Stadium on Saturday (11/21/2026) evening Italian time, or early Sunday (11/22/2026) morning WITA, the Giallorossi led 1-0 as the first half neared its end. 
 Donyell Malen made the difference after scoring in the 39th minute. The Dutch striker put Roma in the lead during a match that was quite open, with both teams having opportunities to score.

 The Parma vs AS Roma match drew attention as it brought together two teams in different situations in the current Serie A standings. Roma is competing at the top of the table, while Parma needs points to move away from the relegation zone. 
 Gian Piero Gasperini's team arrived with a streak of 18 league matches without a loss. Conversely, Parma, coached by Alberto Gilardino, sought to utilize the support of the Ennio Tardini crowd to halt the positive run of the visitors . 
 Flow of the Parma vs AS Roma Match 
 Parma showed courage from the opening minutes. The hosts tried to pressure Roma's defense through the movements of El Bilal Touré and Nesta Elphege, who troubled the Giallorossi backline several times. 
 Roma did not remain silent. Paulo Dybala and Donyell Malen became the focal points of the attack, while Rodrigo Mora played the role of connecting the midfield to the front line. 
 In the early minutes, Parma had an opportunity through Mariano Troilo. However, Mile Svilar was still able to secure the Roma goal. 
 The Serbian goalkeeper experienced some physical discomfort after moving to anticipate an opponent's attack. Nevertheless, Svilar continued the match. 
 Parma threatened again through attacks from the left side involving Emanuele Valeri. His crosses created dangerous situations in front of the Roma goal several times. 
 One of the hosts' best chances came when Touré found shooting space inside the penalty box. However, his attempt was blocked by the visitors' defense. 
 Roma then increased the pressure. Dybala's movement provided more attacking variety, while Malen continued to look for gaps between the Parma defenders. 
 The deadlock was finally broken in the 39th minute. Malen finished the chance with a right-footed shot directed into the Parma goal, giving Roma a 1-0 lead. 
 The goal changed the situation of the match. Parma tried to respond before halftime, while Roma sought to maintain the lead they had gained. 
 Dybala Returns as Starter, Gasperini Relies on Malen 
 The return of Paulo Dybala was one of the main points of interest in this match. The Argentine player was trusted to start from the first minute after recovering from an injury. 
 Gasperini paired Dybala with Malen in the attack. Rodrigo Mora was played as an attacking midfielder, while Bryan Cristante and Manu Koné maintained the balance of play in the midfield sector. 
 Before the match, Gasperini explained that several important players had returned to a physical condition that allowed them to play. 
 "I think they have recovered. They trained well and are back to fitness," said AS Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini in a press conference on Friday, November 20, 2026. 
 Gasperini also emphasized that the competition schedule is still long, so Roma must maintain consistency rather than just thinking about the result of a single match. 
 Dybala's presence gave Roma more options when building attacks. His ability to find space and deliver passes provided important support for Malen, who was moving on the front line. 
 Serie A Standings: Roma Competing at the Top 
 Before the 12th week match, AS Roma occupied third place in the Serie A standings with 27 points from 11 matches. 
 Roma recorded eight wins and three draws without suffering a single defeat. Attacking productivity was one of their strengths with 31 goals, while the defense had only conceded 10 times. 
 That record placed Roma in a tight competition with Lazio and Inter Milan at the top of the Italian League. 
 Conversely, Parma was in 16th place with eight points from 11 matches. They had only collected two wins, two draws, and seven losses. 
 Parma also faced productivity issues. From 11 matches, the team from Emilia-Romagna had only scored nine goals and conceded 17 times. 
 That difference in performance made Roma the favorite on paper. However, Parma still had the opportunity to put up a fight, especially through counterattacks and set-piece situations. 
 Head to Head Parma vs AS Roma 
 The history of meetings between the two teams shows an advantage for AS Roma. Based on official Lega Serie A records, there have been 32 competitive meetings between Parma and Roma that took place at Parma's home ground. 
 Of that number, Roma recorded 16 wins, Parma achieved 10 wins, while the other six matches ended in a draw. 
 In the last 10 meetings in Parma before this match, no game ended in a draw. Roma achieved seven wins, while Parma obtained three wins. 
 The previous meeting at Ennio Tardini took place on May 10, 2026. At that time, Roma managed to defeat Parma with a dramatic score of 3-2. 
 That record serves as psychological capital for the Giallorossi. Nevertheless, the results of previous matches do not always reflect the course of the next meeting. 
 Lineups for Parma vs AS Roma 
 Parma (3-5-2): Giovanni Daffara; Enrico Delprato, Mariano Troilo, Franco Carboni; Sascha Britschgi, Giovanni Fabbian, Vincent Sierro, Mandela Keita, Emanuele Valeri; El Bilal Touré, Nesta Elphege. 
 Coach: Alberto Gilardino. 
 AS Roma (3-4-1-2): Mile Svilar; Gianluca Mancini, Leonardo Balerdi, Mario Hermoso; Edoardo Lulli, Bryan Cristante, Manu Koné, Nahuel Molina; Rodrigo Mora; Paulo Dybala, Donyell Malen. 
 Coach: Gian Piero Gasperini. 
 The match was officiated by referee Simone Sozza, assisted by Vittorio Di Gioia and Mattia Politi as assistant referees. Aleandro Di Paolo served as the VAR. 
 Roma Seeks to Maintain Momentum 
 The match against Parma had significant meaning for Roma, who were trying to maintain pressure on their rivals in the race for the top position in Serie A. 
 Before this match, Roma recorded 18 consecutive league matches without a loss, consisting of 14 wins and four draws. 
 Roma also had a positive away record after being unbeaten in their last eight league matches outside of home. 
 For Parma, this match was an opportunity to measure the team's progress against one of the candidates for the top of the table. 
 Roma's one-goal lead until the end of the first half did not guarantee the match result. Parma still had the opportunity to respond, while Roma had to maintain concentration so as not to lose momentum. 
 The final result of the Parma vs AS Roma duel will influence the competition at the top as well as the battle for important points in the lower zone of the 2026/2027 Serie A standings.
